reason: The cited evidence supports the alloy's baseline strength, ductility, density, and BCC structure (E1), and confirms the HR50CR70 + rapid annealing processing route (E2, E3). However, no cited passage provides evidence for the formation of a bimodal grain size distribution, its effect on dislocation mobility or grain boundary stability, or the oxidation/corrosion resistance of this alloy. The key mechanistic premises linking microstructure to oxidation and the bimodal trade-off are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Ti65(AlCrNbV)28Zr7 is a lightweight (~5 g/cm³) single-BCC MEA with >1000 MPa yield strength and >20% ductility in as-cast state
Hot rolling (HR50) plus cold rolling (CR70) and rapid annealing can refine microstructure and improve ductility
A bimodal grain size distribution can be engineered by HR50CR70 + rapid annealing at ~850 °C for 30–50 s
Bimodal grain structure simultaneously enhances dislocation activity (strength/ductility) and stabilizes grain boundaries against oxygen ingress
Excessively fine grain size leads to intergranular oxidation, creating a trade-off in oxidation resistance
